<!-- All news items below this line -->{{Current events|year=2007|month=04|day=19|content=

* [[Virginia Tech shooting]]:
** [[Tim Kaine]], the [[Governor of Virginia]] announces an inquiry into the massacre. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/6574513.stm (BBC)]
** University officials confirm that the students killed during the massacre will all be [[Posthumous recognition|posthumously]] awarded their degrees during commencement ceremonies. [https://web.archive.org/web/20100407025518/http://www.dailymail.com/story/News/2007041927/Virginia-Tech-to-award-victims-posthumous-degrees (Charleston Daily Mail)]
* The [[prime minister of Norway|Norwegian prime minister]] announces that the government has agreed to unilaterally [[Energy_in_Norway#Carbon_emissions|cut Norway's carbon emissions]] by 30% by 2020, and proposes [[carbon neutrallity]] for [[2050]]. [http://www.regjeringen.no/en/dep/smk/primeminister/Prime-Minister-Jens-Stoltenberg/Speeches-and-Articles/2007/Speech-to-the-congress-of-the-Labour-Par.html?id=463749 (Norwegian Government)]
* [[Joseph Nacchio]], the former [[Chief Executive Officer]] of [[Qwest Communications]], is found guilty of [[insider trading]] for stock sales worth tens of millions of dollars made in 2001. [http://money.cnn.com/2007/04/19/news/newsmakers/nacchio.reut/index.htm?section=money_latest (CNN Money)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* The United States holds talks with [[NATO]] and Russian officials over plans to deploy a [[missile defence]] system in Europe. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/6570533.stm (BBC)]
* The [[Prime Minister of Australia]] [[John Howard]] states that the [[Murray–Darling basin]] faces an "unprecedentedly dangerous" [[water]] shortage and that [[irrigation]] for farmers will be cut off unless there is significant rain in the next 6–8 weeks. [https://web.archive.org/web/20071209054435/http://www.abc.net.au/news/newsitems/200704/s1901202.htm (ABC News Australia)]
* An [[Amnesty International]] report claims that the attacks on [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] [[civilian]]s by the [[Taliban]] are widespread and systematic. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/6568561.stm (BBC)]
* [[Super Junior]] and two of the group's managers are victims of a [[Cho Kyuhyun#April 2007 car accident|car accident]]. Four of the group's members were injured.
